3. A fully paid equivalence with weighted all-matchings approximation

Define

$$Z(A)=\sum_{M\text{ matching}}\prod_{ij\in M}A_{ij}
=\sum_{k=0}^{n}m_k(A),$$

where $m_k(A)$ is the total weight of the $k$-edge matchings. In particular,

$$m_0(A)=1,
\qquad
m_n(A)=\operatorname{per}(A).$$

Consider the following second algorithmic statement:

For every explicitly encoded nonnegative rational bipartite matrix $A$ and rational $0<\tau\le1$, compute rational enclosures for $Z(A)$ of ratio at most $1+\tau$, deterministically in polynomial bit work jointly in the complete input length, matrix dimensions and $\tau^{-1}$.

This statement is equivalent to the permanent FPTAS in your question. The following constructions prove the equivalence without cancellation or an exact-real oracle.

3.1 From an all-matchings FPTAS to a permanent FPTAS

First perform the exact zero test. Assume

$$p=\operatorname{per}(A)>0.$$

Any positive perfect-matching term is at least $2^{-B_A}$, so

$$p\ge2^{-B_A}.$$

Every partial-matching weight is at most $2^{B_A}$. A partial matching can be described by one choice in $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ for each row, where zero denotes unmatched. Therefore there are at most $(n+1)^n$ matchings, and

$$Z(A)\le2^{B_A}(n+1)^n.$$

It follows that

$$\frac{Z(A)}p\le Q,
\qquad
Q:=2^{2B_A}(n+1)^n.$$

Construct the integer

$$t=\left\lceil\frac{8Q}{\epsilon}\right\rceil.$$

Because $t\ge1$,

$$\begin{aligned}
t^{-n}Z(tA)
&=p+\sum_{k<n}m_k(A)t^{k-n}\\
&\le p+\frac{Z(A)}t\\
&\le(1+\epsilon/8)p.
\end{aligned}$$

The lower bound $t^{-n}Z(tA)\ge p$ is immediate.

Suppose the hypothesized all-matchings algorithm returns

$$L_Z\le Z(tA)\le U_Z,
\qquad
U_Z\le(1+\epsilon/4)L_Z.$$

Return

$$\boxed{
L=\frac{L_Z}{t^n(1+\epsilon/8)},
\qquad
U=\frac{U_Z}{t^n}.
}$$

Then

$$L\le p\le U,$$

and

$$\frac UL
\le(1+\epsilon/4)(1+\epsilon/8)
\le1+\epsilon.$$

Costs and dynamic range

The large numerical fugacity is fully represented:

$$\operatorname{bits}(t)
=
O\!\left(
B_A+n\log(n+1)+\operatorname{bits}(\epsilon)
\right).$$

Furthermore,

$$\operatorname{bits}(tA)
\le B_A+O(n^2\operatorname{bits}(t)),
\qquad
\operatorname{bits}(t^n)=O(n\operatorname{bits}(t)).$$

Constructing $Q,t,tA,t^n$, and the final rational divisions, takes polynomial bit work. There is no interpolation, subtraction of nearly equal quantities or hidden exponential-size integer.
